skill.name: nodejs-backend-patterns
skill.description: Build production-ready Node.js backend services with Express, Fastify, middleware patterns, authentication, database integration, and API design guidance.
skill.summary: Create structured Node.js backend services with practical Express, Fastify, database, authentication, and API patterns.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript imports, and normal environment configuration examples. One static network finding is confirmed because the Fastify example binds to all interfaces, and semantic review found unsafe dynamic SQL, permissive CORS, and unbounded Redis key deletion guidance.

remediation.issue: Dynamic SQL update builder uses request body keys as column names.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist writable fields and map them to fixed column names before building the SET clause.

remediation.issue: Fastify CORS example allows arbitrary origins.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit allowed-origin list from configuration and document safe production defaults.

remediation.issue: Cache invalidation uses Redis KEYS and deletes every matched key.
remediation.suggestion: Use SCAN with prefix scoping, validate patterns, and keep broad invalidation internal only.

remediation.issue: Fastify listen example binds to all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Default local examples to localhost and document when 0.0.0.0 is appropriate for container deployments.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Dynamic SQL Column Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: The update flow accepts request body updates and converts their keys into a SQL SET clause without an allowlist. A malicious field name could alter the generated SQL if this pattern is copied into production.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data flow is visible from req.body updates to Object.keys(updates) and direct interpolation into SET ${setClause}. Parameter binding protects values, but not interpolated column identifiers.

semantic_findings.title: Permissive CORS Example
semantic_findings.description: The Fastify setup registers CORS with origin true, which can allow arbitrary origins. Authenticated APIs should restrict origins to an explicit allowlist.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permissive origin setting is explicit. It may be acceptable for limited public APIs, but it is unsafe as broad backend guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Redis Key Pattern Deletion
semantic_findings.description: The cache service accepts a pattern, calls Redis KEYS, and deletes every matching key. This can cause latency spikes or broad cache deletion if the pattern is influenced by untrusted input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The method directly uses a caller-supplied pattern with KEYS and bulk deletion. The risk depends on call sites, which are not shown in the skill.

content.value_statement: Node.js backend projects need consistent structure, secure middleware, and database patterns. This skill provides practical Express and Fastify guidance for production API work.
actual_capabilities: Provides Express and Fastify setup patterns with middleware, logging, compression, and validation guidance.
Explains layered architecture across controllers, services, repositories, models, routes, and utilities.
Shows authentication, authorization, JWT handling, rate limiting, and structured error handling patterns.
Covers PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis caching, transactions, and database connection pooling examples.
Defines reusable API response, dependency injection, and async error wrapper patterns for TypeScript services.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not a complete runnable application.
Requires project-specific validation, secrets handling, authorization rules, and deployment hardening.
Does not include full testing guidance; it refers users to a separate testing skill.
Does not replace a security review for production APIs.

use_cases.title: Design a New REST API
use_cases.description: Plan an Express or Fastify service with routes, controllers, services, repositories, middleware, and response conventions.

use_cases.title: Add Authentication to an App
use_cases.description: Use the patterns to structure JWT login, refresh tokens, password hashing, authentication middleware, and role checks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Backend Architecture
use_cases.description: Create shared conventions for service layers, database access, error handling, caching, and production readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic API
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nodejs-backend-patterns to design a simple Express API for users. Include routes, middleware, validation, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Structure Service Layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nodejs-backend-patterns to design a layered Node.js backend for orders. Include controllers, services, repositories, database access, and response patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Add Production Middleware
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nodejs-backend-patterns to add authentication, authorization, request logging, rate limiting, validation, and global error handling to an existing Fastify service.

prompt_templates.title: Review Backend Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nodejs-backend-patterns to review my Node.js API architecture. Identify gaps in middleware, database handling, caching, authentication, and production operations.

output_examples.input: Design a user management API with Express and PostgreSQL.
output: A layered architecture plan with route, controller, service, and repository responsibilities.
Middleware recommendations for validation, authentication, logging, compression, and error handling.
Database guidance for connection pooling, parameterized queries, and user response shaping.

output_examples.input: Add JWT authentication and refresh tokens to an existing Node.js service.
output: A login flow using password hashing, consistent unauthorized errors, and token generation.
Authentication middleware that verifies bearer tokens before protected routes.
Refresh token guidance that should be adapted with rotation and storage controls.

output_examples.input: Improve production readiness for a Fastify backend.
output: A checklist for security middleware, CORS restrictions, structured logging, rate limiting, and health checks.
Database and cache recommendations for pooling, graceful shutdown, retries, and safe invalidation.
Error handling guidance that avoids exposing internal details in production responses.

best_practices: Adapt examples to your project security model before using them in production.
Keep validation, authorization, and database access centralized in clear application layers.
Use environment variables for secrets, but protect them from logs, responses, and client-side exposure.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sample database update builders without allowlisting writable fields.
Do not use permissive CORS settings for authenticated production APIs.
Do not expose internal errors, stack traces, or secret configuration in API responses.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete backend project?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture patterns and examples that you adapt inside your own Node.js project.

faq.question: Can it help with both Express and Fastify?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes setup and middleware patterns for Express and Fastify services.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes JWT login, refresh token, password hashing, authentication middleware, and authorization examples.

faq.question: Does it include database guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis caching, transactions, and connection pooling patterns.

faq.question: Is the guidance production ready as written?
faq.answer: No. Review CORS, SQL update builders, cache invalidation, secrets, and deployment settings before production use.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
